disease_label_per_paper: Strongyloides hyperinfection associated with Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia, meningitis, ventriculitis and gas-forming spondylodiscitis

demographics.country_or_region_context: Singaporean Chinese man with rural childhood exposure

presentation_summary: An 82-year-old Singaporean Chinese man presented with one day of generalized lethargy, malaise, and fever.
He had hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation, long-standing intermittent eosinophilia, and unrecognized continued steroid exposure with hydrocortisone plus prednisolone up to admission.

Initial evaluation showed fever 38.2 degC, generalized tonic-clonic seizure, GCS E1V1M2, WBC 19.2 x10^9/L with neutrophilia, lymphopenia, and low-grade eosinophils, and admission blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecalis.
On hospital day 3 he remained febrile despite cleared blood cultures and had WBC 20.4 x10^9/L with absolute eosinophils 1.65 x10^9/L.
CSF on day 4 showed pyogenic meningitis physiology with protein greater than 2.00 g/L, glucose 2.3 mmol/L, and WBC 173 cells/uL, though cultures were negative after antibiotics.
Strongyloides stercoralis larvae were detected in stool and early morning nasogastric aspirate; stool remained positive from day 4 through day 8.
MRI brain showed ventriculitis; CT and lumbar MRI showed bilateral pneumonia, L3/L4 gas-forming spondylodiscitis, left psoas myositis/phlegmon, and small gas-containing abscesses.
He received antibiotics, daily ivermectin through a nasogastric tube, and one dose of albendazole, but died on hospital day 11.

actual_treatment: intravenous ceftriaxone, ampicillin, and acyclovir were started for meningoencephalitis coverage
phenytoin and lorazepam were used for seizure management
acyclovir was stopped after negative viral testing while ceftriaxone and ampicillin continued
oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg/day was administered daily through a nasogastric tube from day 4
antibiotics were broadened to cefepime, metronidazole, and ampicillin during persistent fever and deep-focus evaluation
one dose of albendazole 400 mg was given on day 10
psoas abscess drainage was not performed because abscesses were small and the patient was coagulopathic

outcome.source_text_value: patient died on day 11 despite microbiologic clearance of bacteremia and later negative parasite samples

quality_warnings: Strongyloides larvae, IgG, and post-treatment clearance are confirmatory or microbiology context; they are not ordinary symptom evidence.

Enterococcus species identity is preserved in microbiology; generic blood-culture positivity and CNS/deep-focus complications are also mapped because bacterial translocation is a real hyperinfection pathway.
CSF culture negativity is interpreted in the context of prior antibiotic treatment, as described by the paper.
Remote eosinophil values are kept in lab_trajectories with approximate day offsets to preserve the long prediagnostic pattern.
